newsOverlay.marketBias: Oil/Hormuz and rates risk remain elevated: Brent traded around $107 while the U.S. 10-year yield remained near multi-year highs; CPI remains inside 24h / PREPARE VOLATILITY

items.headline: Brent trades around $107 as inflation and rate-hike concerns remain elevated
items.summary: Reuters reports Brent around $107 as disrupted Hormuz and Red Sea supply routes keep oil prices elevated, while Treasury yields remain near multi-year highs and markets price a high probability of a Fed hike next week. This is a continuation of the existing HIGH macro risk regime rather than a distinct new catalyst.
items.whyItMatters: Persistent triple pressure from oil, yields and tighter policy expectations can constrain crypto liquidity and increase downside volatility.
items.actionReason: The latest oil move extends the already-recorded macro risk regime but does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: Brent reaches $105.26 and WTI moves above $100 as tanker attacks escalate
items.summary: Reuters reports Brent rose about 4% to $105.26 and WTI moved above $100 for the first time since May as attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea intensified. The escalation extends the oil-supply shock and increases inflation, yields and risk-asset volatility pressure.
items.whyItMatters: A renewed oil spike above $100 for both Brent and WTI can lift inflation expectations and bond yields and tighten financial conditions for crypto and other risk assets.
items.actionReason: This is a material macro escalation but not a direct crypto protocol failure and does not independently justify REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW.

items.headline: ECB raises deposit rate by 25 bp to 2.50%
items.summary: Reuters reports the ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.50%, its second hike of 2026, as energy-driven inflation remains above target. The decision tightens European financial conditions; Lagarde's press conference remains relevant for near-term volatility.
items.whyItMatters: A higher ECB policy rate can pressure global risk assets through yields, FX and tighter financial conditions.
items.actionReason: The scheduled decision is resolved, so its pre-event AVOID NEW ENTRY window no longer applies; post-decision repricing can still produce volatility.

items.headline: US August PPI rises 0.4% m/m and 5.4% y/y
items.summary: Reuters reports U.S. producer prices rose 0.4% in August, in line with market expectations, while the annual rate increased to 5.4% from 4.8% in July. Energy prices rose 4.2%, keeping inflation and Fed-rate sensitivity elevated ahead of CPI.
items.whyItMatters: The monthly print was expected, limiting surprise risk, but the higher annual rate and energy contribution keep inflation pressure material for Fed expectations and crypto liquidity.
items.actionReason: The pre-release AVOID NEW ENTRY window has ended; CPI on September 11 is now the next major inflation catalyst.

items.headline: ESMA warns of abrupt market-correction risk and deeper crypto-finance linkages
items.summary: Reuters reports ESMA warned that elevated valuations, deteriorating macro indicators and geopolitical stress increase the risk of an abrupt market correction, while deeper crypto integration with traditional finance could amplify systemic linkages. The warning is supervisory context rather than a direct market action.
items.whyItMatters: A major EU securities regulator is explicitly flagging cross-market correction risk and growing crypto-traditional-finance interconnection.
items.actionReason: Material context, but not a direct regulatory restriction or asset-specific event.

items.headline: Nasdaq to invest $100 million in Kraken parent Payward
items.summary: Reuters reports Nasdaq's venture arm will invest $100 million in Kraken parent Payward to deepen collaboration on tokenized-equity trading infrastructure. The move is a meaningful institutional-adoption data point but does not create a Crypto Reca buy signal.
items.whyItMatters: A major traditional exchange operator committing capital to crypto market infrastructure signals deeper institutional integration.
items.actionReason: Positive institutional adoption is contextual only and never creates a buy signal.

items.headline: Brent holds above $101 as Asian equities weaken and U.S. yields remain near 2023 highs
items.summary: Reuters reports Brent around $101.4 in early Asian trading while benchmark U.S. 10-year yields hold near 4.8406%, after reaching their highest since 2023. Asian equities weakened as markets continued to price the oil-driven inflation and rates shock ahead of U.S. inflation data.
items.whyItMatters: The persistence of $100-plus oil and near-multi-year-high long yields keeps global financial conditions restrictive for crypto and other risk assets.
items.actionReason: Continuation of the active macro risk regime; no independent REDUCE REVIEW or EXIT REVIEW trigger.

items.headline: EIA raises 2026 Brent forecast as Middle East shut-ins drain global oil inventories
items.summary: The U.S. EIA says global oil inventories have fallen by about 400 million barrels so far in 2026 and forecasts average Middle East crude shut-ins of 5.7 million b/d in 4Q26. It now forecasts Brent to average $91/b in 2026, with traffic constraints through Hormuz continuing through the fourth quarter.
items.whyItMatters: Persistently tight oil supply and depleted inventories can keep inflation expectations and long yields elevated, tightening financial conditions for crypto and other risk assets.
items.actionReason: Extends the duration of macro risk but is not a direct crypto failure.

items.headline: Brent rises above $100 as Middle East conflict escalates
items.summary: Reuters reported Brent above $100 per barrel for the first time since July 24 as Middle East conflict escalated and Hormuz traffic fell sharply.
items.whyItMatters: A sustained oil move above $100 can tighten financial conditions and increase volatility across crypto and other risk assets.
items.actionReason: Material macro escalation, not a direct monitored-asset failure.

items.headline: Strive discloses purchase of 1,375 BTC at an average price of about $79,281
items.summary: A Strive SEC filing dated September 8 states the company purchased 1,375 bitcoin from August 31 through September 4 at an average price of approximately $79,281 including fees and expenses.
items.sourceName: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Strive 8-K
items.whyItMatters: A 1,375 BTC corporate purchase is a meaningful institutional-flow data point.
items.actionReason: Positive institutional accumulation is contextual only and never creates a Crypto Reca buy signal.

items.headline: Houthi attacks disrupt Saudi energy facilities and wound at least 73
items.summary: Reuters reports Houthi attacks struck several Saudi cities and caused fires at energy sites; Saudi Arabia's energy ministry confirmed operations at some energy installations were halted.
items.whyItMatters: Confirmed disruption at Saudi energy installations broadens the Gulf supply-risk channel.
items.actionReason: Material macro/geopolitical escalation affecting energy infrastructure.

items.headline: Liquid Network attacker returns 3,400 BTC after bridge-node patch; about 598.5 BTC remains with actor
items.summary: The Block reports the actor returned 3,400 BTC to the Liquid federation address after Blockstream said bridge nodes were patched, while about 598.5 BTC remained with the actor.
items.whyItMatters: Returning roughly 85% materially reduces the immediate loss tail but does not fully resolve infrastructure risk.
items.actionReason: Major risk reduction, not a buy signal.

catalysts.headline: U.S. Consumer Price Index for August 2026
catalysts.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics schedules the August 2026 CPI release for September 11 at 8:30 a.m. ET (14:30 Madrid).
catalysts.whyItMatters: CPI is a major input to Fed expectations, Treasury yields, the dollar and crypto liquidity.
catalysts.actionReason: The HIGH event is inside 24 hours; positive or negative data remains contextual and cannot create a buy signal.

catalysts.headline: Federal Reserve FOMC rate decision, SEP and press conference
catalysts.summary: The Federal Reserve calendar confirms the two-day FOMC meeting on September 15-16, with the policy decision at 2:00 p.m. ET and press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET on September 16.
catalysts.whyItMatters: The rate decision and projections can materially reset yields, the dollar and global crypto liquidity.
catalysts.actionReason: Reliable HIGH catalyst inside the next seven days but not yet inside the 24-hour volatility window.
